newsitem.title: FRANCE: Historian says some Nazi camp gas made in France.
newsitem.headline: Historian says some Nazi camp gas made in France.

text.p: A French historian said in interviews published on Tuesday that some of the notorious Zyklon B poison gas used to kill millions of people in Nazi concentration camps was produced in France.
Annie Lacroix-Riz said she found that the French chemical company Ugine produced Zyklon B when associated with German firms during the 1940-1944 occupation of France.
She told the centre-left daily Le Monde and the Communist daily L'Humanite that her efforts to publish the findings in official journals were consistently thwarted.
The French steelmaking giant Usinor Sacilor, which took over Ugine in 1972, said in a communique that its current activities "had no connection with the allegations contained in these articles".
Nazi-hunter Serge Klarsfeld told Reuters: "Many commercial firms in occupied Europe worked, willingly or not, for the Nazi war effort.

"I don't think one should attach too much importance to this development. It is obvious that the Germans who ordered Zyklon B from Ugine didn't say they were going to use it for homicidal purposes and simply ordered it under the term "pesticide,' its initial use."
